inputs.share_count_basis: 844,169,318 fully paid shares: 844,433,596 at 31-Mar-2025 (750.6m + 93.8m rights shares, then partly paid) less 264,278 forfeited and cancelled in FY2026 after the final call (FY2026 AR note on equity share capital). No dilutive securities remain: FY2026 basic and diluted EPS are both 22.32. Paid-up capital of INR 169 crore at INR 2 face is unchanged at 30-Sep-2026. Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The July 2019 1:2 bonus is already in the history.
inputs.net_debt_basis: REPRESENTATIVE, not a balance-date figure: the simple average of the March trough and the September peak. 31-Mar-2026: borrowings 220,460 (non-current 155,350 + current 65,110) less cash 59,750, other bank balances 1,110 and current investments 6,340 = 153,260. 30-Sep-2026: borrowings 327,150 (109,260 + 217,890) less 32,680, 640 and 6,980 = 286,850. Average 220,055. UPL's working capital peaks in H1 (inventory +74,890 in H1 FY2027) and unwinds in Q4, so the March figure management quotes (about 1.6x EBITDA) is the annual low and the September figure (about 3x) the high; the unlevered flows carry no charge for the debt carried between those dates, so the bridge takes the mid-point. Lease liabilities (15,250 at Sep-2026) are excluded because lease cash is charged in the flows. Receivables sold under non-recourse factoring are derecognised and not added back; the FY2026 AR does not quantify the outstanding balance, so net debt is understated by an unknown amount.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, share based payments add-back (INR 70 crore); no net-share-settlement tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes 0 throughout)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z NSE regular session, final minutes of Friday trading
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built, 11.5% in every scenario. Cost of equity about 13.7% (India 10-year G-sec about 6.8% + beta 1.1 x mature-market ERP plus India country premium of about 6.3%); pre-tax cost of debt about 8% (largely USD bonds and loans swapped or carried against INR depreciation; S&P BB at UPL Corp, CRISIL/CARE AA+ domestically), about 6.2% after tax; weights about 68/32 equity/debt on market capitalisation against the representative net debt. Flows are INR-translated USD/BRL/EUR receipts, so terminal growth of 4.0-5.0% is nominal INR (global crop-protection growth of 2-3% in USD plus long-run INR depreciation). Cyclicality, leverage and restructuring risk are carried in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a WACC premium, and the rate does not vary by scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2026 repayment of lease liabilities including interest was INR 641 crore (1.24% of revenue), charged through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (INR 1,530 crore at Mar-2026, 1,525 at Sep-2026) are excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A excluding right-of-use depreciation (3,244 - 578 = 2,666 crore, 5.14% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge; the flows are consolidated (100% of subsidiaries). Minorities hold roughly 22% of UPL Corporation (ADIA, TPG), about 22% of Advanta (KKR and others) and 9% of UPL SAS. Book NCI is 65,940 at Sep-2026 (the USD 400m perpetual that used to sit inside NCI was redeemed in H1 FY2026). Book understates the claim: minorities took 18-19% of group profit in FY2022-FY2023 and 13% in FY2026. The bridge therefore deducts 17% of the base-case pre-NCI equity value rather than book. The deduction is a fixed amount, so it over-deducts in the bear case and under-deducts in the bull case; see key_risks_to_valuation.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Company EBITDA (FY2026 INR 9,588 crore, 18.5%) excludes other income and the recurring 'exchange difference on trade receivables and payables' line (INR 316 crore in FY2026, 0.6% of revenue). The model's ebitda_margin_path is company EBITDA less that FX line: FY2026 actual 17.9%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (INR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in the bridge, matching-asset rule). UPL is an operating agrochemical and seeds company, so the default route applies; no memory entry existed (first valuation). BASIS: consolidated group as a going concern. The Composite Scheme of Arrangement (UPL SAS merged into UPL Limited, India crop protection demerged into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions, to be listed separately) and the Advanta offer-for-sale IPO are both pending (CCI approval June 2026, exchange observation letters July 2026; shareholder and NCLT approval outstanding) and no effect is given to either. They are treated as a catalyst and a risk in the narratives, not modelled as post-split entities; an Advanta sell-down would raise NCI and cut debt, roughly value-neutral at fair price. OWNER FCF: reported FCF 54,490 = OCF 78,550 - capex 24,060; finance costs and lease payments sit in financing, so this is pre-interest and pre-lease. last_fcf deducts SBC only (interest income is not stripped: the group is in net debt, and interest received is in investing, not OCF). The forward build additionally charges lease cash of 1.24% of revenue and taxes EBIT at a normal unlevered rate, so year-1 FCF sits below last_fcf. FY0 component check: model EBITDA 92,720 - leases 6,410 - SBC 700 - D&A ex-ROU 26,660 = EBIT 58,950; at 21% tax NOPAT 46,570; + D&A 26,660 - capex 24,060 = 49,170 before working capital. Five-year average reported FCF (FY2022-FY2026) is 45,700, including the FY2024 destocking year (-1,730) and the FY2025 rebound (83,790). WORKING CAPITAL: net working capital is about 16% of revenue at the March trough with factoring; wc_capture is -25% of incremental revenue (growth consumes cash). SBC is 0.14% of revenue, so house and street nearly coincide. Share repurchases: none since the FY2023 buyback (13,550); the flat count is funded by convention, the amount is immaterial. PRICE: the quote is from the last minutes of the 13-Nov-2026 NSE session; refresh at the next close.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (14.1%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (6.0%) and EPS (-9.3%). Equity was lifted by the FY2025-FY2026 rights issue (about INR 3,380 crore) and by INR-depreciation translation gains in OCI (INR 3,546 crore in FY2026 alone), not by retained earnings, so it is rejected as the growth anchor in favour of the 5-year revenue CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; SBC was nil before FY2022): FY2021 50,900, FY2023 52,580, FY2026 53,790. End-point CAGRs hide the cycle: FY2024 owner FCF was -1,800 and FY2025 83,400 on working-capital release. FY2023 to FY2026 revenue is still 3% below the FY2023 peak in INR despite about 15% INR depreciation over the period.

base.growth_note: Year 1 is below the 7-11% FY2027 guidance: H1 FY2027 revenue grew 3.8% and Q2 fell 1.3%, so the guided range needs low-double-digit H2 growth. Later years are nominal INR.
base.margin_note: Model basis (company EBITDA less the recurring trade FX line). Year 1 corresponds to about 19.1% on the company's definition, i.e. EBITDA growth of about 9-10% against the 10-14% guide (H1 +10.6%). Matures at 19.5% (about 20.1% company basis), below the 20-22% of FY2018-FY2023.
base.tax_note: Unlevered rate on EBIT. Cash tax paid ran 12-15% of EBIT in FY2022-FY2023 with a large interest shield and offshore structures; ramped to 22% for Pillar Two and the Indian place-of-effective-management disputes.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 recovery holds but FY2027 lands at the bottom of guidance: global crop-protection volumes stay soft through H2, Advanta and SUPERFORM carry the growth, and revenue rises 6% against the 7-11% guide. Chinese active-ingredient oversupply eases gradually as export rebates go, so pricing stops falling without recovering to FY2022-FY2023 levels; mix shift toward differentiated and biological products lifts the model EBITDA margin from 17.9% to 19.5% by year five, still short of the 20-22% the group earned before the destocking cycle. Working capital keeps absorbing a quarter of each incremental rupee of revenue. The demerger and the Advanta IPO complete without changing consolidated economics.
scenario_narratives.bull: The channel is fully destocked, China's anti-involution policy and rebate removal produce a real price recovery in generic actives, and UPL's innovation pipeline reaches the targeted 20%+ innovation rate, so margins return to the pre-FY2024 range (21.5% model basis, about 22% company basis). Latin America grows volume on acreage, Advanta compounds in the low teens with DECCO, and tighter working capital (-22% capture) converts more of the growth to cash. The crop-protection demerger and Advanta listing close, proceeds retire debt and the conglomerate discount narrows, though the model takes no re-rating beyond a 15x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese generics keep undercutting on price, low grain and oilseed prices hold farmer spending down, and the West Asia shipping disruption keeps input costs high: revenue grows 2-4% in INR (flat or falling in USD) and the margin slides back to 16%, between the FY2024 trough (12.8%) and FY2025 (17.4%). Inventory and receivables consume more cash, the seasonal debt peak near 3x EBITDA becomes the refinancing constraint with INR 9,573 crore of long-term debt maturing inside twelve months, and the restructuring stalls at NCLT or completes on terms that leave more debt with the listed parent. Equity value is highly geared to this outcome because net debt and minorities take about three-quarters of enterprise value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the equity sits behind seasonal debt that reaches about 3x EBITDA at the September peak, the industry pricing cycle is outside UPL's control, and H1 FY2027 is already running below revenue guidance. Base stays at 50%: it is the FY2026 turnaround continuing at a slower pace than guided. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things at once: a Chinese-supply-driven price recovery, delivery of the innovation-rate target, and a clean demerger plus Advanta listing.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical, leveraged generic agrochemical group valued on consolidated unlevered owner FCF at an INR WACC, with leases charged in the flows, minorities and seasonally averaged net debt deducted in the bridge. Debt and minorities absorb close to half of base-case enterprise value, so per-share value is very sensitive to the margin path: the spread between bear and bull is wide by construction and the scenario weighting, not the base case alone, is the number to act on. No value is assigned to a post-demerger re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net debt is a judgment: the March trough (153,260) would add about INR 79 per share and the September peak (286,850) would remove about INR 79 relative to the average used. Non-recourse factoring is unquantified and sits outside all three figures.

NCI is deducted as a fixed 95,000 (17% of base pre-NCI equity) against a book value of 65,940; at book the value per share is about INR 34 higher in every scenario. The fixed amount over-deducts in the bear case and under-deducts in the bull case.

Pending Composite Scheme of Arrangement and Advanta IPO: the listed entity an investor holds will change, debt allocation between UPL Limited and UPL Global is not final, and an Advanta offer-for-sale raises NCI while reducing debt. Not modelled; consolidated going-concern basis only.
Margin cyclicality: a 1 point shift in the whole EBITDA margin path is worth roughly INR 75 per share in the base case, about 13% of value.

Company EBITDA excludes recurring trade FX losses and the reported cash flow is flattered by factoring and by an interest tax shield; the model corrects the first and third but cannot correct the second.
Indian tax authorities' place-of-effective-management proceedings against three overseas subsidiaries are unprovided.
